Package neqsim.thermo.characterization

Class RefineryViscosityBlend

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.characterization.RefineryViscosityBlend
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class RefineryViscosityBlend extends Object implements Serializable
Immutable mass-basis kinematic-viscosity screening result for a refinery blend.

The empirical Refutas relation transforms each source kinematic viscosity to a viscosity blending number, mixes those numbers by normalized mass fraction, and applies the analytical inverse. Every contributing viscosity must be resolved at the same caller-supplied temperature. This class does not mutate an assay or thermodynamic system. Roundoff at a source bound is clamped to that bound, preserving blends of equal-viscosity sources.

  • Method Details

    • fromMassBasis

      public static RefineryViscosityBlend fromMassBasis(double[] sourceMasses, double[] sourceKinematicViscositiesCSt, double temperatureCelsius)
      Create an empirical mass-basis viscosity blend at one explicit common temperature.
      Parameters:
      sourceMasses - non-negative source masses in any common mass unit
      sourceKinematicViscositiesCSt - source kinematic viscosities in cSt at the common temperature
      temperatureCelsius - common source-viscosity temperature in degrees Celsius
      Returns:
      immutable viscosity blend result
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - for invalid arrays, masses, temperature, or contributing viscosities

    • fromBinaryTargetKinematicViscosity

      public static RefineryViscosityBlend fromBinaryTargetKinematicViscosity(double firstSourceKinematicViscosityCSt, double secondSourceKinematicViscosityCSt, double targetKinematicViscosityCSt, double temperatureCelsius)
      Plan the unique mass-basis binary blend that reaches a target kinematic viscosity.

      The two source viscosities and target must be resolved at the supplied common temperature. The target must lie inside the closed interval formed by the source viscosities. Equal-viscosity sources are rejected because their mass ratio is not uniquely determined.

      Parameters:
      firstSourceKinematicViscosityCSt - first source kinematic viscosity in cSt
      secondSourceKinematicViscosityCSt - second source kinematic viscosity in cSt
      targetKinematicViscosityCSt - target blend kinematic viscosity in cSt
      temperatureCelsius - common source and target viscosity temperature in degrees Celsius
      Returns:
      immutable binary blend result with source-order mass fractions
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - for invalid viscosities, temperature, target interval, or non-unique sources
